policy: A caught product failure must gain a reproducible production-path test/type/lint guard before resolution. These historical defects have executable test guards. New failed runs emit regression-candidates.json and stay red; candidates are not automatically declared fixed or counted as tests. Native guards remain not-run until executed on macOS.

Actual macOS bridge fixtures rejected closed readers because the test assumed Linux writer-POLLERR readiness semantics on Darwin.

The native pipe-stop fixture measured observer resumption rather than the worker callback, so its observed delay could not distinguish actual transport latency from delayed test-executor scheduling; the guard now measures callback completion with the unchanged 500 ms bound.
Independent mutation review showed stop-before-start fixtures did not establish descriptor-closure ordering for an already active native input source.
Actual macOS test compilation printed an internal corrupted-JSON error, then exited zero with Build complete; compiler diagnostics must remain blocking despite that exit status.
Adding a valid WAV native obligation exposed a selftest that assumed the final obligation was device proof; the test must remove each actual evidence tier independently of map order.

Actual concurrent Core execution outlasted the mute fixture's five-second automatic semaphore release, invalidating its still-blocked-reader premise before the observer resumed; the same failure was reproduced with a delayed continuation.

The macOS endpoint fixture failed before obtaining its Python port file; the precise startup cause is unproved. Owned bind/listen readiness and explicit cleanup replace competing startup/helper lifetimes without extending the HTTP deadline.
Native event dispatch removed and rejected an unrelated queued mouse-up after AppKit had already consumed its own release.
The AX readiness fixture rejected a transient unknown role immediately, before its existing readiness budget could resolve a valid button; persistent wrong roles must still never receive a press.
Actual production compilation exited zero after internal compiler errors, but the app build step and aggregate gate accepted the command outcome without inspecting its compiler diagnostics.
The original compiler matcher classified a Swift warning's source excerpt containing an error: argument as a compiler error.
Independent review reproduced a passing aggregate receipt after inserting an internal compiler error into the final bundle compilation log and refreshing its hash.
Independent static review found the diagnostic header parser no longer rejected LLVM ERROR and absolute compiler-path headers that the previous matcher blocked.

The new CLI regression printed expected error diagnostics into unittest's result line, preventing the strict runner from identifying every reported test. Capture and assert those diagnostics inside the fixture.
Actual AppKit queue insertion narrowed a synthetic event number and rounded its timestamp, so the native journey driver rejected its own queued release as unrelated.
The wrong-ID and wrong-path worker fixtures also used invalid WAV data, allowing unrelated WAV rejection or startup failure to stand in for the intended protocol guard.
A throwing worker fixture removed its directory before cancelling and joining the render task and closing its worker; failed assertions could discard diagnostics while work was still using them.

The closed-pipe fixture accepted a write after local read closure during concurrent Mac process tests. Its bare Pipe could be inherited by another child; a later FIFO poll readiness check was invalid on Darwin. The guard opens a private FIFO with atomic CLOEXEC, proves positive byte transfer, requires ENXIO from a nonblocking writer-open to establish no readers, unlinks it, and requires the exact unavailable error from one tested write.

The SwiftPM async-main drain exited during owned AppKit event dispatch with exit zero and no terminal Swift Testing event. A synchronous AppKit host now owns the three UI processes; the gate still requires their complete qualified execution and exact host/bundle command.

Synchronous Process.run held the voice session actor, delaying cancellation and request deadlines during launch. The guard stalls a real launch, requires prompt cancellation and immediate replacement rejection, then proves late-child cleanup.
An expired request could still spawn after waiting for the launch executor. The guard keeps launch queued until the request expires and requires that the process runner is never invoked.

Polling Process.isRunning after termination did not finalize Foundation run-loop ownership; controlled Linux processes remained retained until post-exit waitUntilExit. The guard requires owned process release after confirmed child exit.

The foreign-event ownership fixture queued its release before an async layout wait; the normal AppKit loop legitimately consumed it during that yield. The guard now settles through the public click path, then inserts the foreign event and invokes the same synchronous dispatcher without yielding, requiring the exact foreign release to remain queued.

AppKit native mouseDown tracking consumed a preexisting foreign release despite the driver never dequeuing it directly. Admission now refuses any preexisting release before posting or dispatching a gesture, preserving exact identity and action count; a clean subsequent click remains required.

Onboarding film playback was only gated by window attachment, leaving hide, minimize and occlusion without explicit pause. Real-player lifecycle guards require positive advancement before native visibility transitions and paused media afterward.

A multi-film preview accepted completion from any AVPlayerItem with the same asset URL, allowing another player to grow its queue. Completion now requires an exact owned item and is consumed once; a foreign same-URL item cannot requeue.

A nested private observable fixture failed native test compilation because the observation macro emits a file-scope conformance extension. The fixture uses file-visible scope; the required native compiler barrier and actual onboarding journey remain mandatory.

A synthetic accessibility fixture annotated the ignored NSButton wrapper and changed its role while the exposed NSButtonCell remained unmarked. The fixture now annotates the actual cell with natural positive role and rejects an explicit wrong role on that same exposed element.

Mac Swift concurrency checking rejected Notification values captured across MainActor.assumeIsolated in decorative-player callbacks. Observers now extract only Sendable item identity and notification-kind values, while owned player access stays on MainActor; the native compiler barrier and real lifecycle guard remain required.

A failure-only native accessibility diagnostic treated NSWindow.accessibilityIdentifier() as Optional although its AppKit declaration returns String, preventing the test target from compiling. It now uses the declared type and retains the exact synthetic-window prefix check; the native compiler barrier and accessibility journey stay mandatory.

Native Sendable conversion callbacks captured a mutable fed flag and a borrowed non-Sendable PCM buffer without an explicit owner. A per-conversion read-only buffer owner now serializes consume-once state and distinguishes live input starvation from final end-of-stream.

The Sendable resampler held a mutable AVAudioConverter without a conversion ownership boundary. A nonblocking guard now rejects overlap: live conversion drops that failed chunk and checked file conversion throws, while a later uncontested conversion still succeeds.

The hosted Mac image enables Reduce Motion, so real decorative-film tests incorrectly required movement in a profile where the app correctly pauses. A wrapper now configures normal motion only in the disposable GitHub-hosted profile, restores the existing boolean, preserves test failures, and requires fresh native NSWorkspace verification before owned-window tests. Product accessibility policy is unchanged.

A managed-runner motion setup must never report native success if restoring the original accessibility preference fails. The wrapper fails closed on restore errors and refuses local, self-hosted, unknown or non-Mac environments before touching preferences.

A real onboarding film could be ready, visible and eligible yet remain paused at its first presentation after attachment. FilmView now resynchronizes through the existing playback policy at the AppKit drawing boundary, retaining all visibility, Reduce Motion and disposal gates. The original real-playing guard remains mandatory.

A timed-out verification command was killed only at its direct driver, leaving an inherited process group able to keep working or retain output. The executor now owns a fresh group, signals it without reaping the identity between TERM and KILL, and bounds direct-child cleanup; an unrelated control group must remain alive.

Interrupted polling or external child reaping can make a process-group identity unsafe to signal and can lose the real exit status. The verifier refuses nondefault SIGCHLD before launching and does not signal a reaped or uncertain child group.

Accepting an exit result without checking the monotonic clock after poll can classify completion beyond the deadline as a passing check. Late observed completion now remains timeout124 and cannot trigger a signal to a reaped group.

Synthetic Kokoro fixtures hardcoded the Apple developer-tool Python launcher, which did not enter Python before the original deadline on either fresh runner. CI now selects the exact Xcode interpreter for synthetic fixtures only. The real production worker script must still publish only a complete acknowledged WAV within the unchanged fixture deadlines.

An invalid explicitly configured test interpreter must not silently fall back to another executable or create a fixture. Selection now rejects missing, nonexecutable, directory, relative, empty and NUL paths; the validated choice is shared by both fixture launch sites.

The outer cleanup-test supervisor raised PermissionError during its back-to-back TERM/KILL teardown on macOS after the runner behavior assertions. The fixture now sends one SIGKILL to its unreaped owned group before a bounded reap; no production runner assertion is relaxed.
A cleanup fixture must not hide unexpected signal denial or reap failure while closing its pipe handles. These errors remain test failures rather than becoming successful cleanup.

Native host artifacts identified the host but omitted the dynamically loaded test-bundle bytes. A prelaunch input sidecar now records that digest so crash evidence can reject changed or redirected compiled input.

A crash from another process, another launch or an ambiguous crashed thread must not be used to diagnose the original native failure. Only exact owned-host identity and bounded sanitized frames can be emitted.
A collector refusal with a pre-existing output directory could overwrite its result during finalization. Existing output and original failed test evidence must never be overwritten.
Malformed or nonfinite crash JSON, including exponent overflow, must not enter a diagnostic or weaken its identity bounds. Unsupported report content remains unavailable evidence.

ISO-only parsing rejected the documented Apple IPS date form with a space before the numeric UTC offset. Exact Apple report timestamps and ISO host telemetry now match with explicit timezones; timezone-less input stays invalid.
Valid SSE completion finalized the inner scene stream twice and rejected every complete response.
A projected later cue could repair an invalid earlier visible checkpoint before validation.
Applying individual operations instead of the whole cue rejected valid forward references and violated cue atomicity.
Replay omitted spoken-only revision reservations, causing later valid scene cues to fail or skip revisions.
Freezing an interrupted animation as an ordinary edit pushed a never-displayed future target into undo history.
Switching partial audible playback to manual captions could rewind elapsed media time.
Manual caption replay included end cues with an earlier media position.
Individually finite nested group scales could overflow native rendering transforms.
Safe animation endpoints could interpolate an unsafe composed parent/child transform.
An admitted animation longer than its actual audio beat could stop at a partial pose while history held its unseen target.
Reduced Motion exposed intentionally hidden static objects before their later reveal cue.
Settings generation drifted from the checked-in production catalog, removing existing options and changing behavior.
Stale settings generation re-enabled voice capture opt-ins by default.
Settings generation could expose or drop the intentionally hidden debug microphone-conflict bypass.
A duplicate settings row could conceal an earlier unsafe capture default.
Renderer group visibility and connector bounds ignored transformed descendant state.
Renderer Reduced Motion forced static reveal to one, exposing objects before admitted cues.
An old push-to-talk release could finish a replacement capture without an attempt identity.
A shortcut-started pending microphone attempt could survive control disable or window loss.
Immediate press/release before the asynchronous start task ran could start microphone capture after release.
An occluded window could pause its display link while narration continued, leaving visual cues stalled until completion.
Synthesized PCM could carry nonfinite sample values to native playback.
Independent callback tasks did not formally preserve start-before-finish for short clips and could accumulate unbounded clock samples.
Queued old playback observations needed epoch invalidation and bounded control-message overflow behavior.
WhisperKit download:false could still fetch tokenizer resources; installed-file readiness was not a no-download capability.
A whitespace/newline-only model passed the existing completeness predicate before being trimmed to an empty request model.
Credential header construction needed bounded keys and rejection of all C0/DEL controls.
Request construction needed independent snapshot identity, nonempty-byte and delivered-dimension bounds.
A global sidebar-save error could be cleared by another conversation while the failed link remained unsaved.
Retained AppKit panels could hide without SwiftUI onDisappear, so narration needed an explicit owned-window stop hook.
ChatStore skipped visual-only conversations because they had no messages, orphaning scene history after restart.
Replay could include accepted future beats that were never presented before interruption.
A failed explanation write could lose its only retained snapshot when switching conversations or reopening while disk remained unreadable.
Retry could enqueue an older failed checkpoint behind a newer in-flight save, producing a persistent stale replacement conflict.
A different record saving successfully could hide an unresolved save failure.
Switching back before a debounced save completed could create a second history record for one Chat; blank opens must remain unsaved.
A rejected Chat switch could leave another conversation’s private history active for submission under the newly selected Chat.
A failed initial load left its conversation ID selected and prevented retrying the same conversation after recovery.
New explanation work could be admitted during asynchronous quit saving and be lost after the quit decision.
The unsaved-record cap blocked recovery of already-owned failures as well as new record creation.
Listing only decodable histories could falsely report that a corrupt linked record was deleted; exact typed absence must be idempotent.
Unreadable records with unknown ownership cannot be declared deleted or removed indiscriminately.
A first meaningful visual edit while storage was unavailable could remain unlinked and be orphaned when the scratch Chat changed.
Stopping a reopened explanation during deletion could attempt to recreate the just-deleted Chat link.
Seeking could cancel future synthesis but leave a queued future beat buffering indefinitely; current-beat previews must stop at their bound.
Deleting an ordinary Chat must not initiate explanation storage work or block quit for an unrelated storage root.
Retention could evict a still-open history while the controller retained its persisted checkpoint, causing the next edit to use stale save preconditions instead of safely recreating the owned record.

An owned NSButtonCell invoked its retained synthetic target exactly once but returned false from accessibilityPerformPress, causing the readiness fixture to reject an action it had observed. Only that fixture may acknowledge the exact single action without retry; disabled controls and the production AX driver remain strict.

Numeric explanation diagnostics must not report caption-only presentation as audible output or count read-only replay as a new generation; exported counters must retain their actual lifecycle and media boundaries.

The diagnostics collector labeled task_vm_info.phys_footprint as resident bytes, misrepresenting the provided process-memory metric. Numeric reports must name physical footprint explicitly and must not export the old resident-byte keys.

The first native build found ambiguous inference in the locked synthesis-cancellation tuple. Explicit optional tuple types and self-qualified members now enforce the cancellation snapshot at compile time; the existing cancellation fixture exercises its owned PCM cleanup after compilation.

The first native build found mixed CGFloat and Double arithmetic in chart layout. Explicit CGFloat conversion at the drawing boundary now makes chart/timeline coordinate expressions type-check; the production Canvas fixture remains bound to the compiled renderer.

The first native build inferred a String-keyed SceneKit options dictionary, making the shorthand rendering-API key invalid. The explicit SCNView.Option rawValue now enforces the SDK key type; the owned native SceneKit fixture exercises construction after compilation.

macOS history fixtures threw unsafePath under Foundation-normalized temporary roots; the original log did not identify the rejected component. Disposable fixtures now use throwing POSIX realpath, following the existing Darwin system-alias test pattern, and verify every directory component without following symlinks. Production path rejection remains strict.

macOS renderer run at 9d7dcfa failed the group-highlight assertion because SceneKit stores emission intensity as Float, so the production 0.4 read back as 0.4000000059604645 against an exact Double comparison. Production highlight reached the child correctly; the assertion now requires the material and compares within 1e-6.

The failure-only own-PID accessibility snapshot called AXUIElement from a detached background task. AppKit serves own-process AX requests on the calling thread, so SwiftUI built its accessibility tree off the main thread and trapped (Incorrect actor executor assumption, SIGTRAP exit -5), crashing the test host and erasing the original UI failure. The snapshot now runs synchronously on the main actor with the same node, depth, time and per-element timeout budgets, own PID and owned-window marker rules, and the original failure remains reported.

Live QA of the packaged CI preview crashed on onboarding's voice step: SFSpeechRecognizer.requestAuthorization's handler, written inside @MainActor PermissionsModel, inherited main-actor isolation and Swift 6 trapped when TCC called it on a background queue. Chat microphone, voice, Polyglot and Focus requests had the same shape; all now await the nonisolated SystemAuthorization helper.

Live QA of the packaged CI preview crashed on the first provider-logo render: Bundle.module traps in Zeus.app because SwiftPM's accessor looks beside the app while scripts/bundle.sh seals Zeus_Zeus.bundle in Contents/Resources. EngineBrandImage now uses ZeusResources.bundle.
The packaged preview shipped a test-target resource bundle (Zeus_ZeusCoreTests.bundle with a fixture) inside Zeus.app because bundle.sh copied every SwiftPM resource bundle.

Zeus requested Location (onboarding weather row) and Focus status (Proactive) with no NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription or NSFocusStatusUsageDescription in Info.plist; macOS terminates an app that requests a protected resource without its usage string.
Transcribing a file while the microphone was open overwrote the listening phase, so the recorder kept capturing under a phase that no longer allowed finishing it.
A cancelled or superseded file transcription still finished: the first of two overlapping files marked the second done and a cancelled file overwrote the clipboard.
A late Parakeet progress callback after the download finished left the progress bar stuck and refused every later download.
A failed Parakeet download was retried on every dictation key press with no terminal state.
A double click on Turn on for Microphone and Speech Recognition (or a second talk-key press, or two Chrome steps on one site) raised the consent prompt twice.
A slow update-feed check begun before auto-update was turned off finished late and brought the update badge back.
A microphone-test level queued from a finished test landed in the next test and inflated its peak, giving the wrong verdict.
The Record page opened empty with a disabled Record button: nothing listed displays or selected one until the owner clicked Load displays, and that load needed Screen Recording permission.

Opening Settings froze the window: Settings drew rows from calls that wait on the system (the Launch at login switch asked SMAppService on every render, Integrations rows read hook files on every render, and window open read the disk, the microphone list and a TCC-protected folder on the main thread), and a subprocess wait held a Swift concurrency thread.

Instant commands depended on a Laya local decision server that is not installed by default: a probe and a 20 second start wait sat in front of the model stage. Laya is removed and Jev (key plus a monthly limit, 600 ms budget) is the only model stage; a saved Laya or Auto choice now maps to Jev.

The Show in screen sharing switch looked broken: while a meeting was active (exactly when a screen is shared) the policy forced every Zeus window hidden even after the owner chose to show Zeus. The owner's explicit show now wins over the meeting auto-hide; the default stays hidden and the teleprompter's private session still hides. The closed notch light also sat partly behind the camera housing; Top bar position now lowers the closed bar, light, ticker, wings and screen-edge glow together.

Live QA of build 0405391: with no ElevenLabs or OpenAI key and Kokoro not installed the reply was spoken with the default macOS voice Samantha and no Ultron effect. The Mac voice is now the deepest male voice, never Samantha, and plays through the effect chain.

Engine routing had no logged reason and preferred one engine regardless of availability. Auto now orders ElevenLabs, OpenAI, Kokoro, Mac voice, skips paused engines and always ends with the Mac voice.

The Ultron effect was an amplitude wobble applied only to some engines. The chain is now pitch, EQ, distortion, comb and room, scaled by intensity with 60 percent as the default and tasteful wet limits.
Voice replies could run to four sentences. A spoken reply is now one to three sentences.
A technical error such as a failed brain route could be spoken. It is now replaced by an in-character plain line.
A fresh install did not guarantee the Ultron persona with the effect on at 60 percent.

Talk to Zeus took 85 s and said nothing (owner run of build 0405391): four engines were tried one after another with 20 to 30 s silent timeouts, the Claude CLI launched with the owner's hooks, plugins and claude.ai connectors on every call (its help probe used a GUI PATH that cannot find ~/.local/bin, so even --strict-mcp-config was dropped), Codex ran the account's large default model, and an Ollama probe plus warm-up wait sat before the first request. A turn now starts every fast engine at once (Haiku or GPT-6-Luna class), speaks the first to stream, stops the rest, says one short filler at 900 ms, fails with one spoken error inside 8 s, and runs a Sonnet deep answer behind it as a follow-up.

The spoken-turn latency fixes could silently regress: a sequential engine loop, a network probe or warm-up wait before the first request, a first-text budget above 8 s, a voice Claude launch without --safe-mode, or a help probe through /usr/bin/env.
Closing the welcome guide before the last step recorded nothing, so the guide reopened by itself at the saved step on every launch.
A background Automation check that began before the person clicked Allow finished later and overwrote the new grant, deleting the saved grant until the next refresh.
Settings Automation Allow more did nothing when the only open app was already allowed, never named the apps to open, and failed silently for an app macOS had refused.
A Polyglot input that ended while the run was still starting was counted as open, so the run showed Listening on a dead microphone or stopped a two-input run early.
Stopping Polyglot and starting it again quickly let the first run's late start stop the second run's microphone.
A second final result while the speech recognizer was restarting opened a second recognition task for the same dictation turn.
When the Hey Zeus listener could not start it retried every 10 or 30 seconds forever and logged the same failure each time, with no needs-attention state.
A microphone level queued just before the teleprompter ended landed after the reset and lit the meter again.
A feature that asked twice for Accessibility was started twice when access arrived, and a feature turned off while waiting kept the 3 second poll running forever.
The first of two overlapping Beamer commands or connection refreshes to finish cleared the busy flag while the other was still running.

UltronEffectGraph connected its effect nodes to the engine's main mixer before the engine had a usable output. On a Mac with no audio device, an unusual format or a changed device AVFAudio raised an uncatchable Objective-C exception (setFormat error -10868) and ended the app, or the whole test process on CI. Connection now validates the format and output first, offline rendering enables manual mode before connecting, the live chain connects lazily and a refusal falls back to passthrough or no audio with a logged reason.

Onboarding footer: the Languages step had its own Set up later and Continue buttons in a separate switch branch, so while a step animated the outgoing and incoming pairs existed together (duplicate controls, a tap could reach the previous step's action), and Set up later on Languages bypassed the skip event of the progress state machine. One shared footer now serves every middle step.
A talk-to-Zeus fast answer that broke off mid-sentence left its background deep answer running and able to be spoken after the broken one.
Engines stopped because another engine won the race reported a cancellation error that was logged, ranked as a failure in the latency book and could be counted against quota state.
A voice turn cancelled by a new key press finished later and cleared turnRunning under the turn that replaced it, so the wake word and busy checks saw an idle assistant mid-answer.

A hands-free silence timer from an earlier turn released the talk key while the owner was holding it, and a wake-word turn left the previous answer's deep follow-up and speculative run alive to speak over it.

Pressing the talk key or Esc while a voice engine was mid-request counted as that engine failing and could pause a healthy ElevenLabs, OpenAI, Kokoro or Chatterbox route; a line rendered after the interruption still played.
Alert timers kept running while the notch peek or panel covered the capsule, so alerts expired without ever being seen.
Dismissing the last alert under the pointer left the stack hovered, so the next alert never started its auto-dismiss clock.
A snoozed alert was dropped for good when the notch was open at the moment it came back ten minutes later.
The Record countdown kept running after the owner left the Record page, then started a screen capture they could no longer see or cancel with Escape.
A Record countdown whose display or window disappeared ended in a silent no-op instead of saying the source was gone.
A background Launch at login status read that began before the owner flipped the switch landed afterwards and put the switch back.
A background hook-file look that began before Connect or Disconnect overwrote the click's result, and Connect for Codex never updated the AI connections row until the next look.
Desktop pointing shipped off with no draw-while-held setting although the owner chose Control+Option and draw while held as the defaults.
Scribe call-window names had no first-run default and could have been read without the owner's existing Accessibility grant.
The alert Reply button only opened the item, the same as Open, for apps that have no reply target.
Invitee names and per-turn voices were memory only, so after a relaunch the recap had no invite names and no Remember this voice button.
The Dismiss button and Stop could leave a pinned Polyglot bar stuck, and the pin decision was spread over the notch with no pure contract.
On macOS older than 26 Polyglot reported translation as unavailable for the language pair, hiding the real reason.
The Language packs and Speaker recognition cards could be defined without being placed on any Settings page, so the features were unreachable.
A process of another user, or a program other than the Zeus app on the browser bridge socket, could connect to the agent and browser sockets: the files were only mode 0600.
A hook client could send a bundle ID of its own choosing and have Zeus launch that app, or label a risky command low risk.
A model-written action could start a coding agent, or send a prompt to ChatGPT, Claude or Dust, without an approval card.
The update feed accepted http, file and app-scheme addresses, and its download link was opened whatever its scheme.
The system HUD monitor woke ten times a second for as long as the app ran, whether or not a HUD was shown.
Zeus pinged Ollama and the cloud API at launch and at every wake from sleep, before anyone used voice.
Transcribing with Parakeet when its model was missing started the model download without any click.
A call-window name was bound to a voice on weak evidence: two people lit about equally over one voice.
Call-window evidence overwrote a speaker name the person had typed.
A muted participant tile could win the vote for a voice and name it.
One call-window name landed on two different voices.
A name the person declined for a voice was offered again for that voice.
French call-window labels (parle, micro coupe, Invitee, Vous) were not understood, so no name was found.
Where a speaker name came from was lost when a meeting was reopened, so an automatic name looked typed.
Merging two speakers could not be undone.
Pruning tiny voices folded a named speaker or the owner into someone else, or could not be reversed.
Assigning selected words to another speaker lost or overlapped the block time.
A circle or underline drawn around a control mapped to no target, so ink never selected what the user meant.
Spoken 'this' and 'that' reached the model with no link to what the pointer or ink showed.
A mark stayed on screen after the control it pointed at moved, changed or closed.
The Fn+Control dictation preset overwrote the dictation key with no way back, and its collisions were not reported.
Alerts for Spotify, Chrome, Notion, Dropbox, terminal and meeting apps fell back to a generic glyph because only one bundle id was tried.
Pointing ink only appeared while dragging, so tracing a control while the keys were held left no trail and no stroke.
Holding the pointing keys put a mouse-capturing overlay over the screen, so clicks and focus did not reach the app being asked about.
A modifier release that the key stream never reported left a pointing turn open indefinitely.
Sleep, wake or a display change during a hold or a turn left the hold armed and marks on stale geometry.
The ring could land off the candidate on a 2x display or a display with a negative origin.
The pointing Accessibility hit test ran on a detached background task, which this process's own AX rule forbids.
The per-turn trace line could carry free text; it must hold only mark names and millisecond offsets.
A 3D edit written for an older scene revision was applied to the current scene instead of being rejected, so a follow-up could change parts the model had not seen.
A 3D edit naming a part that does not exist could create a second copy or half-apply with its neighbours instead of rejecting the whole change.
3D spins and flows advanced per rendered frame, so speed changed with the display rate and a stalled display jumped the animation.
An energy marker's direction could depend on the camera angle, so an orbit could reverse what an arrow meant.
World-anchored 3D labels could overlap each other or cover another label's anchor as the camera orbited.
Malformed 3D operations (unknown commands, out-of-range numbers, bad references, extra fields) were not all refused before reaching a renderer.
Drivetrain wheels turned against the direction of travel in the demonstration, so the car appeared to roll backwards.
A rejected 3D edit left the turn running with a half-built scene instead of ending it with the last valid scene kept.
A chart value axis had no ticks, units or gridlines, and a range such as 3 to 1003 gave no readable scale.
Nice-number ticks left floating-point residue or broke on fractions and huge magnitudes.
A bar chart could start away from zero without saying so, exaggerating differences.
Non-finite, zero-span or overflowing chart data could reach drawing and produce NaN pixels.
A timeline spaced events evenly while presenting itself as a time axis.
Chart numbers carried no provenance, so invented values could read as measured or live.
The chart axis wire fields were not version gated, so a v1 or v2 turn could carry them, and unknown axis fields were not rejected.
An axis spec with a bad domain, tick hint, units or live timestamp was accepted.
The desktop card could cover the pointed-at target, the pointer trail or the active input area.
Card placement assumed a display at the origin and broke on negative display origins.
The card fallback shrank a diagram below a readable scale instead of splitting into beats or going speech only.
A late callback from a replaced or cancelled turn could show or update the desktop card.
The desktop card could take key or main status from the app the owner was using, or be interactive beyond its close control.
The production card honoured a stale turn token and stayed on screen after its turn ended.
A spoken turn had no timing: nobody could tell where the 85 s went. Every voice turn now writes one voice-latency line with stage times and the engine and reason, and never the transcript or a key.
scripts/voice-latency.sh could not report p50 and p90 for key-up to first audio, so a speed claim could not be checked on the real app.
Brains and the persistent Claude process warmed at launch instead of when the talk key went down.
A long first sentence with no comma was spoken only after its full stop. The first twelve complete words now go to the voice at once.

The direct Anthropic request used an old Haiku, no prompt cache block and left thinking on. It now sends the current Haiku with thinking off, low effort and a cached system block, and retries plain forms only on 400 or 404.
Every CLI-only spoken turn paid process start. A lean persistent claude process is reused, recycled after a few turns, and replaced when its flags change.
Sentences joined with a click: each sentence started and ended at a non-zero sample. A 4 ms fade is applied at a buffer edge only where needed.
An ElevenLabs answer could change model, and so timbre, between sentences. One model is pinned for the whole answer and Studio falls back to the fast model only before any audio plays.
The Ultron voice was designed automatically on first use. A voice is created only after Tony taps Create Zeus voice.
Saving an ElevenLabs key gave no feedback. A quick check now says Key works or why the key was refused, without echoing the key.
The spoken persona rules (at most three sentences, lead with the answer, never menacing) and the no-filler-when-fast rule had no test.
The macOS fallback voice ignored the language of the reply and no hint offered an Enhanced or Premium voice when only basic voices were installed.

The light around the screen no longer hugged the screen edge and the notch felt delayed: an automatic top bar drop (30% of the notch height) applied to every notched display, lowered the volume and brightness glow and the edge wave off the real screen corners, and slid the closed bar on every open and close. The drop is now 0 until the owner moves the slider, the edge lights always follow the physical edge, and the edge lights, voice glow, voice ring and avatars draw on the display clock instead of 30 or 60 fps timers.

Dictation start and stop sounds were missing or late: the start cue played only after the microphone had opened, the stop cue only after transcription and paste, and meeting mode counted Zeus's own microphone as a call and muted both.
Scribe dropped the person's microphone for the whole meeting whenever another app (a call app, a browser or an unknown app) was using it, and recorded only system audio.
Once any other app had used the microphone, a latch kept Zeus's microphone excluded for the rest of the app's life, across recordings, even after that app let go.
The shared-microphone state could stay set after the other app stopped using the microphone; it now clears on the next reading and on stop.
Hey Zeus kept the microphone open during calls captured by helper processes (browser audio or WebKit helpers, call-app helpers) because the conflict check only matched exact app bundle IDs.
Output ducking restored the volume onto whatever device was default at the end, leaving the original device lowered, and quitting while ducked left the Mac's output at the lowered volume.
A spoken to-do kept the microphone open indefinitely after its page or the bar closed, with no time limit.
Closing the prompter while its recording was still starting left the camera and microphone recording with nothing able to stop them.
